findings.text: follow-on: the safety argument ends "The 300 s ini default governs only direct pytest runs outside the launcher" but omits the two mechanisms that actually protect a non-lane run -- conftest.py _SLOW_FILES excludes tests/test_equilibrium_forward_solve.py from the default -m "not slow" lane, and scripts/nova_lane/standing_suite.sh lists it in GPU_FILES so the standing suite routes it to the 3600 s lane -- so the line leaves a bare CPU pytest run reading as exposed to the 300 s bound when the repository already excludes and routes the file.

follow-on: the manifest states "Confirm H200 lane job 1280612 ran ... --timeout 3600 (launcher-injected default)", but confirm-lane-forced-3600.log's own header names SOURCE_REVISION=4a441e717, the commit carrying @pytest.mark.timeout(660), and pytest-timeout's marker overrides the command-line --timeout, so the 660 mark and not the launcher's 3600 governed the tested node and the shipped head 3ec60184d was never run under the lane's own bound.

follow-on: the measurement ran on a compilation-cache miss (PINNED_REVISION_MISMATCH pinned=eb565ed4 serving=8b149152a) with no cache-guard receipt because the guard plugin never loaded, so the 312.57 s accelerator-route wall is compile-inclusive and an upper bound rather than a warm-lane wall; this strengthens rather than weakens the no-mark conclusion, but the manifest's "measured wall" is not a warm-cache measurement.

follow-on: no negative-control arm completed -- negative.log's job 1280623 was CANCELLED at 2026-10-03T15:06:12 with no test result and the coordinator cancelled the earlier negative job 1280617 by id -- so the manifest carries a negative_control_waiver rather than a red log; the waiver is sound for a measurement-only node that lands no check, but four cancelled negative logs remain in /home/ITER/mcintos/.cache/nova-forward-solve-timeouts/ with no result.

gate_arms_note: The reviewed run is measurement-only and its manifest names no baseline_suite or after_suite field, so the count is derived from the two gate logs it does declare in its test_logs line. Arm A: ~/.cache/nova-forward-solve-timeouts/measure.log (job 1280609, SOURCE_REVISION=8b149152abd28de233465cc189c9f2ae0fc5defb, command pytest -p no:cacheprovider tests/test_equilibrium_forward_solve.py --timeout=0 --durations=0 -m 'slow or not slow') 29 passed, EXIT_STATUS=0, completed=true, failure_ids=[]. Arm B: ~/.cache/nova-forward-solve-timeouts/confirm-lane-forced-3600.log (job 1280612, SOURCE_REVISION=4a441e7179c4f641aea9a5327d12c0597568691e) 1 passed, EXIT_STATUS=0, completed=true, failure_ids=[]. Both declared arms are green. Independently, git diff 8b149152abd28de233465cc189c9f2ae0fc5defb..3ec60184d0a330d00a1d3cf57c06f1406c7a20cd -- tests/ is empty, so the head test surface is byte-identical to the base and no test can be newly failing: added_failure_count=0, added_failure_ids=[]. Caveat a reader must carry: the two arms measure different revisions (base 8b149152a and the marked intermediate 4a441e717), and the shipped head 3ec60184d carries no test change, so this zero bounds no changed test surface -- it is a zero over an unchanged file, which is the correct reading for a node that lands no test change.

item_verdicts.diff: the three commits are 4a441e717 (add the mark, +3 lines), d5ec45fd7 (remove it, -3 lines) and 3ec60184d (the 101-line fragment); the net base..head diff is the fragment alone and touches no product source and no test.
item_verdicts.done_when: the done-when's measure (one H200 lane job over the whole file with --timeout=0 --durations=0) ran as job 1280609 and measure.log records "29 passed, 1 warning in 665.51s" with the slowest item test_the_accelerator_routes_agree_on_the_fixed_point at 312.57 s, EXIT_STATUS=0; the "second job over only the marked node ids" ran as job 1280612 (confirm-lane-forced-3600.log, 1 passed in 378.95 s, EXIT_STATUS=0) but at revision 4a441e717, the commit that carried the @pytest.mark.timeout(660) mark, so it measured the marked tree rather than the shipped head 3ec60184d.
item_verdicts.goal: read the node goal ("Give every forward-solve test that runs past 200 s on the H200 a per-test timeout taken from its measured wall") against the landed head 3ec60184d; the landed change adds no per-test timeout at all, because scripts/nova_lane/run.sh:274 injects --timeout "${NOVA_LANE_TEST_TIMEOUT:-3600}" into every lane pytest run, and the coordinator scope correction in the run directory's resume-3-advice.txt redirected the node to a measurement-only completion.
item_verdicts.manifest: the reviewed manifest.md records status complete, commits 4a441e717/d5ec45fd7/3ec60184d, the fragment as its only changed path, test_logs measure.log and confirm-lane-forced-3600.log, a landing line citing job 1280609 (29 passed in 665.51 s, slowest 312.57 s), a negative_control_waiver in place of a negative_control_log, and a follow_ons entry for the cache guard; the durations it quotes reconcile with /home/ITER/mcintos/.cache/nova-forward-solve-timeouts/measure.log.
item_verdicts.write_paths: git diff 8b149152a..3ec60184d --name-status is a single added path, docs/evidence/fragments/forward-solver-route-integrity/fsri-forward-solve-tests-fit-their-bound.html, inside the three granted write paths; git diff 8b149152a HEAD -- tests/ prints nothing, so tests/test_equilibrium_forward_solve.py is byte-identical to base.

justifications.durability: the node lands no code and no assertion, so nothing can regress and no guard is owed, and the durable artifact is the committed fragment whose per-test table reproduces from measure.log; the cache-guard non-load it records as a follow-on is a real defect left for its owning node rather than a missing guard in this one.
justifications.evidence: /home/ITER/mcintos/.cache/nova-forward-solve-timeouts/measure.log (job 1280609) records 29 passed in 665.51 s with the 312.57 s accelerator-route item and its durations table reconciles with the fragment, but the confirm arm ran at 4a441e717 with the 660 mark governing rather than at the shipped head, and on a compilation-cache miss (PINNED_REVISION_MISMATCH pinned=eb565ed4 serving=8b149152a), so the recorded walls are compile-inclusive and the bound is confirmed only by reading the launcher source.
justifications.fit: the landed artifact is one evidence fragment under docs/evidence/fragments/forward-solver-route-integrity/ named by its capability and matching the plan's fragment idiom, with a table rather than a figure for data that is naturally tabular and no name the repository naming rules forbid.
justifications.goal_fidelity: the shipped head gives no test a @pytest.mark.timeout, the goal's named artifact, because scripts/nova_lane/run.sh:274 already injects --timeout 3600 on every lane pytest run and resume-3-advice.txt redirected the node to measurement-only, so the goal's purpose (no legitimate long forward-solve test is killed by pytest-timeout) is fully met while its literal deliverable is absent from docs/evidence/fragments/forward-solver-route-integrity/fsri-forward-solve-tests-fit-their-bound.html.
justifications.scope_discipline: git diff 8b149152a..3ec60184d --name-status is the single granted fragment path with tests/ byte-identical to base, the reviewed worktree is clean, and all three commit subjects are conventional with bodies and no AI attribution and no plan or sprint identifier.
